body:
## Correction: this pattern is already documented, and partly already counted

I filed this as a new finding. It is not. `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` §3 documents
the hydrate-collapse defect directly, and uses magnesium sulfate as its worked
contrast — the same pair I presented above as novel evidence:

> `MgSO4·7H2O` mapped to `CHEBI:32599 magnesium sulfate` does not say "a hydrate
> of magnesium sulfate"; it says "this **is** magnesium sulfate", and every
> downstream join then treats 246.47 g/mol and 120.37 g/mol as one node.
>
> The contrast is in the data: `MgSO4 x 7 H2O` sits on `CHEBI:31795 magnesium
> sulfate heptahydrate` and is **correct** … `MgSO4·7H2O` is the same substance
> on the generic term, and is the defect.

§3 also already sizes parts of it — "34 hydrate-labelled subjects" on the
compliant pattern, "a further **22** `cas:`-identified hydrate records [with] no
parent row and no registry row … a backlog, not counter-examples", and "32
hydrate families".

So the framing above is wrong in an important way: I presented the notation
split (`x 7 H2O` vs `·7H2O` landing on different terms) as evidence that
matching was arbitrary, when the document already identifies one of those as
correct and the other as the known defect.

## What actually stands

The **measurement**, not the discovery:

- **26 records** whose label names a hydrate while the recorded structure
  contains no water, found by a mechanical check rather than by inspection;
- **10 terms absorbing all 26**, with `CHEBI:34683` carrying five distinct
  `Na2HPO4` hydrates — the multiplicity is the part I have not seen quantified
  elsewhere;
- the **detector itself**, which is cheap and can run as a standing gate.

And §3 already prescribes the remedy, so the triage fork I described is really
just its steps 1–3: specific term if one exists (step 1), else `cas:` primary
with a parent `narrowMatch` and registry row (step 2), else mint
`kgmicrobe.compound:` (step 3). `CeCl3 x 7 H2O` is a step-2/3 case, not a novel
category.

Retitling would be reasonable: this is "measure and close the documented hydrate
backlog", not a new defect class.

Found because a research agent read `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` §3 and applied it as
the standard, which surfaced that I had not.

## Count correction: 38, not 26 — my detector read the wrong field

The detector checked `chemical_properties.formula`. That key does not exist.
The corpus uses **`molecular_formula`**:

```
1466  molecular_formula
1418  smiles
1411  inchi
1514  cas_rn
   0  formula
```

So `formula` was always `None`, and the "does the structure contain water"
test silently fell back to smiles/inchi alone, while the "does this record have
a structure at all" gate excluded every record carrying `molecular_formula` but
no SMILES/InChI.

Re-run against the correct field on merged main: **38 records**, 4 terms
absorbing more than one. The 26 in the issue body is an undercount, not a
different population.

The same typo silently disabled a companion check reported on #324 as "0 hits"
— see the new issue for what it finds once fixed (36 records).

Worth a standing lesson for this repo: `formula`/`molecular_formula` and
`cas`/`cas_rn`/`cas_number` are all plausible-looking names and only one of each
is real. A detector that silently reads a non-existent key reports a clean bill
of health, which is worse than erroring.

## The remaining 12 are blocked on evidence that does not exist

Recording a negative result so this is not re-attempted.

All 12 remaining records state "hydrate" with no number. Each **does** carry a `cas_rn`, so the CAS→PubChem method that resolved #327 and #337 was applicable and was run against all 13 (the 13th is resolved, below).

**Zero of 13 return a formula containing water.** PubChem's entries for these CAS numbers are as stoichiometry-agnostic as the labels:

| record | recorded | PubChem title | PubChem formula |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Stachyose hydrate` | C24H42O21 | `Stachyose hydrate` | C24H42O21 |
| `Adenine hydrochloride hydrate` | C5H6ClN5 | `Adenine hydrochloride` | C5H6ClN5 |
| `a-Ketoglutaric acid disodium salt hydrate` | C5H4Na2O5 | `Disodium oxoglurate` | C5H4Na2O5 |
| `Cefsulodin sodium salt hydrate` | C22H19N4O8S2.Na | `Cefsulodin Sodium` | C22H19N4NaO8S2 |
| `DL-Isocitric acid trisodium salt hydrate` | C6H5O7.3Na | `Isocitric acid, dl-` | C6H5Na3O7 |
| `Chlorhexidine diacetate salt hydrate` | C22H30Cl2N10.2C2H4O2 | `Chlorhexidine Acetate` | C26H38Cl2N10O4 |
| `Fosmidomycin sodium salt hydrate` | C4H9NNaO5P | `Fosmidomycin Sodium` | C4H9NNaO5P |
| `Glycerol phosphate disodium salt hydrate` | C3H7Na2O6P | `Sodium Glycerophosphate` | C3H7Na2O6P |
| `DL-Glycerol 1-phosphate sodium salt hydrate` | C3H8NaO6P | `Sodium 3-phosphoglycerate` | C3H8NaO6P |
| `D-Fructose 6-phosphate disodium salt hydrate` | C6H11Na2O9P | (long systematic title) | C6H11Na2O9P |
| `Bathophenanthrolinedisulfonic acid disodium salt hydrate` | C24H14N2O6S2.2Na | — | no hit |
| `Vancomycin Hydrochloride Hydrate` | C66H75Cl2N9O24.HCl | — | no hit |

Seven agree exactly with the record; two get no hit; the rest differ only in notation (`C6H5O7.3Na` vs `C6H5Na3O7`), not in water content.

So the stoichiometry is absent from **all three** sources available — the label, ChEBI, and PubChem's entry for the record's own CAS. It needs a supplier catalogue or the original recipe text. Anything else would be a fabricated mass in a published field.

## One resolved

`Glycocholic acid hydrate` — CAS `1192657-83-2` resolves to a **verbatim title match** with `C26H45NO7`, exactly one H2O more than the recorded `C26H43NO6`. Applied in #345.

Flagging a wrinkle rather than burying it: `CHEBI:182320`, itself labelled *"Glycocholic acid hydrate"*, records the **anhydrous** `C26H43NO6`. So the record now diverges from its own `EXACT_MATCH` term. PubChem was preferred because its value is tied to the specific registered substance the record's CAS denotes, whereas a ChEBI term named "hydrate" carrying an anhydrous formula is the same modelling gap as #342. **If #342 concludes ChEBI's hydrate handling should be taken at face value, this record should revert** — the evidence note on the record says so explicitly.

## Correction: the residual was understated — 26, not 13

My earlier counts on this issue used a detector with a regex bug and were too low. Correcting the record.

The pattern was `\bhydrate\b`. **"monohydrate", "tetrahydrate", "hexahydrate" have no word boundary before "hydrate"** — the preceding character is a letter — so the detector only ever matched ` x N H2O`, `·NH2O` and the free-standing word "hydrate". Every record spelled with a multiplier prefix was invisible to it.

Re-measured with `hydrate\b`:

| | count |
|---|---|
| residual reported earlier (buggy pattern) | 13 |
| **actual residual** | **26** |
| never seen by any earlier pass | 13 |

The 13 missed records:

    2-Keto-D-gluconic acid hemicalcium salt monohydrate
    Cadmium acetate dihydrate
    Chromium(III) Chloride Hexahydrate
    D-Galacturonic Acid monohydrate
    Disodium phosphate heptahydrate (0.02 M stock)
    Esculin Monohydrate
    Galactose 1-phosphate dipotassium salt pentahydrate
    Gly-Gln monohydrate
    L-Malic acid disodium salt monohydrate
    potassium citramalate monohydrate
    Sodium glutamate monohydrate
    Sodium hypophosphite monohydrate
    b-Mannan borohydrate reduced carob seed

Four are fixed in #348 on the standard already used here (label states the stoichiometry; recorded formula is byte-identical to the parent term's): `Chromium(III) Chloride Hexahydrate`, `D-Galacturonic Acid monohydrate`, `Esculin Monohydrate`, and `Sodium glutamate monohydrate` (adopted verbatim from its ChEBI term).

## Two further detector flaws worth knowing before trusting any count here

1. **`b-Mannan borohydrate reduced carob seed` is a false positive.** "Borohydrate" ends in `-hydrate` by spelling alone and is not a hydrate. Now excluded in `add_water_of_hydration.py`.

2. **A combined formula masks the water.** The detector asks whether the formula contains `H2O` notation, but `Gly-Gln monohydrate` carries `C7H15N3O5` — which *is* the monohydrate (`C7H13N3O4` + H₂O), just written combined rather than as `.H2O`. It was corrected back in #326 and is still being counted as defective. So the 26 is itself an over-count by an unknown margin.

Anyone reducing this issue further should fix the detector first: match `hydrate\b`, exclude `borohydrate`, and compare the formula's **element totals** against the parent's plus *n*·H₂O rather than looking for the literal string `H2O`. Counting by string match is what produced both errors.

## Formula defect closed — `missing: 0`

#349 replaces the string-matching detector with element-total arithmetic and takes the missing-water count to **zero**.

The count was wrong every time I reported it on this issue, in four independent ways — all from asking whether a formula *contains the string* `H2O`:

1. `\bhydrate\b` never matched `monohydrate` (no word boundary after a letter) — **24 records invisible**
2. `borohydrate` is not a hydrate
3. combined notation masks water: `Gly-Gln monohydrate` = `C7H15N3O5` *is* `C7H13N3O4` + H₂O — **10 records**
4. `InChI=1S/Cu.H2O4S/...` contains `.H2O` as part of the **sulfate** fragment, so every sulfate hydrate looked already-correct — **which is why all 16 stragglers were sulfates or selenites**

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| missing | 16 | **0** |
| ok | 110 | **126** |
| unknown | 44 | 44 |

The **44 unknowns are the real residual** and are not a defect count: their labels state no stoichiometry, and I verified that neither ChEBI nor PubChem's entry for each record's own CAS supplies it. They need a supplier catalogue or the original recipe text. That figure stayed stable through every correction above, which is the one reassuring thing in this sequence.

`scripts/check_hydrate_water.py --check` now exits non-zero on regression, and 31 tests pin each bug against the values that exposed it — including `Cobalt chloride hexahydrate`, where formula == term formula is *correctness*, not a defect.

The identity half of this issue (hydrates sharing their anhydrous parent's identifier) was closed in #341, and the predicate question in #342/#348.

Two more records in this class, found by cross-checking CultureBotAI/CultureMech#272: filed as #374 (7 hydrate records on anhydrous terms where ChEBI **has** the specific hydrate — §3 step 1, no minting needed) and #375 (a hydrate label resolving through a synonym to the anhydrous record's term).

Worth noting #374 was found by an **external** cross-check rather than by this repo's own gates. `check_hydrate_water.py` (added in #349) checks whether the *formula* accounts for the water; it does not check whether the *term* does. A record can carry a correct hydrate formula while sitting on an anhydrous term — `FeSO4 x 7H2O` on `CHEBI:75832 iron(2+) sulfate (anhydrous)` is exactly that. A term-level check is the missing half.

## Triage of all 39 §3 violations against ChEBI

Re-measured on the repaired instrument (#461): the cohort is now **39**, not 26. Each was checked for whether ChEBI actually holds a hydrate-specific term for it, because §3 branches on exactly that — re-ground if a term exists, else `cas:` anchor + narrowMatch + Rule B1 row.

| outcome | n |
|---|---|
| exact hydrate term at the stated count | 2 |
| hydrate siblings exist at *other* counts | 29 |
| no hydrate term at any count | 8 |

### 6 are re-groundable now, with no chemistry question open

These are the cases where the candidate's label is the parent's label plus "hydrate" — no inference required:

| record | current (wrong) | correct |
|---|---|---|
| `MgCl2x 6 H2O` | CHEBI:6636 magnesium dichloride | **CHEBI:86345** magnesium dichloride hexahydrate |
| `Esculin Monohydrate` | CHEBI:4853 esculin | **CHEBI:73111** esculin hydrate |
| `Betaine x H2O` | CHEBI:17750 glycine betaine | **CHEBI:91242** glycine betaine hydrate |
| `Citric Acid•H2O` | CHEBI:30769 citric acid | **CHEBI:31404** citric acid monohydrate |
| `L-Cysteine x HCl x H2O solution` | CHEBI:91247 L-cysteine hydrochloride | **CHEBI:91248** L-cysteine hydrochloride hydrate |
| `Fe2(SO4)3 x n H2O` | CHEBI:53438 iron(3+) sulfate | **CHEBI:131387** iron(3+) sulfate hydrate |

`MgCl2x 6 H2O` is also a #334 case: its correctly-mapped sibling `MgCl2 x 6 H2O` (with the space) is already on CHEBI:86345, so this re-grounding merges the shadow onto it.

### A trap worth recording: element-count matching conflates isomers

The obvious way to find these is to match ChEBI formulas by element composition after subtracting water. It works for the inorganic salts and **silently produces wrong answers for the organics**:

| record | element-count "match" | what it actually is |
|---|---|---|
| `Maltose Hydrate` | CHEBI:189432, CHEBI:232797, CHEBI:88379 | alpha-lactose monohydrate, trehalose dihydrate, galactinol dihydrate |
| `DL-Isocitric acid trisodium salt hydrate` | CHEBI:32142 | sodium **citrate** dihydrate |

Maltose, lactose and trehalose are all C12H22O11; citrate and isocitrate are isomers. Composition cannot separate them, and every one of those candidates carries water and matches the parent's formula exactly. This is the #324 shape — a wrong term that passes every automated check — so **neither of those two may be re-grounded**; both need the `cas:` anchor route instead.

(Also noted in passing: `CHEBI:233428 '5-(N-ethyl-N-isopropyl) amiloride'` carries formula `C12H22O11.H2O`, which is not that compound. A ChEBI-side data error, not ours.)

### The remaining 31

- **8 have no ChEBI hydrate term at any count** — `CeCl3 x 7 H2O`, `Cefsulodin sodium salt hydrate`, `Chlorhexidine diacetate salt hydrate`, `Cr2(SO4)3 x n H2O`, `Cu(NO3)2 x 3 H2O`, `K2HPO4 x 3 H2O`, `K2SO4 x 7 H2O`, `Na2SO3 x 5 H2O`. §3 step 2 applies unconditionally; **these are unblocked**, no chemistry question to settle first.
- **23 state a count ChEBI does not carry.** For these the correct action depends on whether the label's number is right, which is #344's question. If it is right, they anchor; if it is wrong, several land on a term that already exists (`MgCl2 x 7 H2O` → the hexahydrate CHEBI:86345; `FeCl3 x 4 H2O` → the hexahydrate CHEBI:86254). So #344 has to be answered before these can be actioned, not after.

### Independent corroboration for #344

All 9 of #344's records are in this cohort, and ChEBI's holdings agree with #344's literature table on every overlapping case — two different sources, same answer. ChEBI is narrower (it has no NiCl2 di/tetrahydrate, no CaCl2 mono/tetrahydrate), so **absence from ChEBI is not evidence a hydrate does not exist**: `MnSO4·7H2O` and `Na2HPO4·7H2O` are both real, ordinary reagents that ChEBI simply lacks. ### Suggested order

1. The 6 re-groundings above — mechanical, evidenced, no open question.
2. The 8 + `Maltose Hydrate` + `DL-Isocitric...` = 10 `cas:` anchors — unblocked for a different reason (no term exists / no term *can* be identified).
3. The remaining 23 — blocked on #344.
